text:
marta-gomez: Heads-up — vuln scan flagged multiple CVEs touching our inference stack: protobuf parsing CVE-2026-0456, sentencepiece RCE CVE-2026-0721, and a FlashAttention kernel OOB write CVE-2026-0802. Need quick triage and patch plan.

vuln-bot: Auto-scan results attached: summary -> protobuf: HIGH (parsing lib used in model load + Triton), sentencepiece: CRITICAL (model tokenizer binaries), flashattention: HIGH (custom kernels used on some GPU nodes). See https://internal.vuln/reports/1800500123

alex_kaplan: Thanks Marta. First pass: map which services use which deps. My notes: vLLM linked with sentencepiece for some tokenizers; Triton containers use protobuf for gRPC/serialization; FlashAttention present in dedicated GPU pool images (pinned wheel).

samir.r: Do we know if the protobuf vuln can be mitigated by disabling unknown field parsing or tightening deserialization? Also, can we avoid using system protobuf at runtime by shipping a patched wheel?

june_chen: From infra side — FlashAttention OOB is the riskiest for data integrity / could crash GPUs. We'll need a canary rollout on a subset of Dedicated nodes before org-wide patch. Timeline?

claire-b: QA checklist: perf baseline, regression tests for model outputs, token-level golden checks for sentencepiece, and end-to-end inference smoke. FlashAttention replacement needs perf comparison vs baseline (latency and p50/p95). I can run canary QA if we have a build.

eng-oncall: Short-term mitigation ideas: 1) Route heavy production traffic to fallback model variants that do not use FlashAttention kernels (lower perf but safer). 2) Pin service images to pre-vuln protobuf for now and block inbound model uploads that trigger sentencepiece parsing. Need RBAC guardrails on model upload UI and audit logs enabled.

alex_kaplan: Good. For RBAC/audit: we should enable write-only roles for model uploads, require SSO, and ensure audit logs capture user id + model checksum. If we alter the upload flow, we must coordinate with compliance for retention.

samir.r: KMS question — any patch or rebuild that touches model artifacts (repacking tokenizers) should not leak keys. We must confirm that our KMS client libs are not impacted and that any new build process uses KMS libs with existing RBAC. @june_chen can infra run a KMS smoke?

june_chen: Yes. I'll run KMS smoke and key access audit in the canary cluster. Will check HSM/KMS call patterns and key usage logs.

sre-bot: Deploybot scheduled: canary window suggested 2026-04-02 02:00-06:00 UTC. Will create canary batch of 4 nodes, automatic rollback on OOM/crash or latency > 2x baseline.

marta-gomez: Proposed owners & next steps: alex -> triage protobuf & sentencepiece dependency updates; june -> infra canary + KMS smoke; claire -> QA canary tests; samir -> mitigation scripts and temporary upload RBAC changes; eng-oncall -> traffic routing policy for fallback. I'll open a tracking JIRA and assign.

vuln-bot: Created ticket INFSEC-7890 and attached scanner output + suggested CVSS mapping.

claire-b: One more — we need to validate model signature verification on upload to avoid poisoned tokenizers. Add a step to the upload pipeline: verify checksum + refuse unknown tokenizer types.

alex_kaplan: For protobuf patching: plan is to vendor a patched protobuf wheel into Triton images, run canary, then roll to remaining clusters. If build affecting vLLM appears, we'll test with both system and vendored protobuf to see behavior.

samir.r: Workaround for sentencepiece: re-tokenize models offline in a sandbox container (no KMS secrets mounted) and publish sanitized tokenizer bundles. That buys time while we update libs.

eng-oncall: I'll prepare a traffic-shift playbook: stepwise 10%->30%->60%->100% over 2 hours with abort conditions. Add additional audit logging during the rollout (model id, node id, user).

marta-gomez: Great. Action items captured in INFSEC-7890. Let's reconvene in #eng-runtime after initial canary results. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Note: remember to update release notes for Dedicated customers and post a notice in the Console about the canary window.

claire-b: I'll post results and perf diffs to the ticket.

alex_kaplan: If anyone needs quick repro steps for FlashAttention issue, run the stress harness:
```
./bench_flash.sh --model gpt-medium --tokens 2048 --iters 1000
```
Watch for kernel OOB logs: "kernel: flash_attn_oob_write" in dmesg.

marta-gomez: Thanks everyone. Will follow up with timeline + final approvals.
